name: Saint John Chrysostom
history: The greatest preacher of the early Church, called Chrysostom, golden-mouthed, for his eloquence. Priest at Antioch and then archbishop of Constantinople, he preached the Scriptures verse by verse, defended the poor and rebuked the luxury of the court. He died in exile in 407. Eastern Christians still celebrate the Divine Liturgy that bears his name.
life: John was born at Antioch around 347 and studied rhetoric under the famous pagan teacher Libanius. After his baptism he lived as a monk and hermit in the hills until his health gave way. Ordained priest in 386, he preached in Antioch for twelve years, and his homilies on Genesis, Matthew, John and the letters of Paul are still read. In 398 he was made archbishop of Constantinople, almost against his will. He cut the expenses of the bishop’s household, founded hospitals, called the clergy to holiness and spoke plainly against the wealth of the powerful while the poor went hungry. He made enemies, among them the Empress Eudoxia and Theophilus of Alexandria, and was deposed and exiled twice. Marched in harsh conditions toward the Black Sea, he died at Comana in 407. His last words are recorded as glory be to God for all things.
prayerTo: Saint John Chrysostom, you preached the word of God without fear and saw Christ in the poor at the church door. Pray for all preachers, that they may speak the truth with love, and for me, that I may honour Christ in the Eucharist and in those who are hungry, and give thanks to God for all things. Amen.
penance: Read and ponder one chapter of Saint Matthew’s Gospel today, on which John preached at length, and give the price of one small luxury to the poor.
meditation: Chrysostom warned his people not to honour Christ in church with silks while neglecting Him naked and cold outside. Where is Christ waiting for you beyond the church door today?
